overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by requiring remote attendees to display their full name to attend the November 19 meeting, but found no violation in the abrupt end without a vote to adjourn.

allegations.summary: The Chair told remote attendees they would be removed from the Zoom meeting unless they displayed their full first and last name, a condition on attending the open meeting.
allegations.key_passage: By repeatedly informing members of the public that they would be removed from the Zoom meeting—which was the only method for accessing the November 19 meeting—if they did not display their full first and last name, Chair Rosa placed an impermissible condition on attendance at the meeting and violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The meeting ended abruptly after a platform failure without a vote to adjourn, which the complaint said violated the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require a vote to adjourn the meeting of a public body.

remedy: We order immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
